newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia defends exporters from dumping charges.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia defends exporters from dumping charges.

text.p: Indonesia said on Monday it was concerned anti-dumping procedures against some of the country's exporters were being used as forms of protectionism.

"We must ensure that our exporting firms do not suffer from disguised protectionism through misuse of anti-dumping procedures," Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo told a conference on the impact of anti-dumping laws.
He gave no details of cases in which the government believed anti-dumping laws had been wrongfully enforced.
On the issue of foreign firms dumping products in Indonesia, Tunky said Indonesia's policy would be "in tune with the spirit and letter of the multilateral rules".
But as a developing country, Indonesia must take care that its huge consumer market was not victim to foreign companies which broke World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules on dumping, he added.
"Foreign manufacturers...are often bigger and better established than our own emerging manufacturers. That is why we must also have our own anti-dumping procedures," Tunky said.
